title: SDK parity: customer communications plan (release notes, migration guide, deprecations, announcement)
creator: Henry Cho
body:
## Context
We are standardizing SDK behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go for auth resolution, retries/backoff, timeouts, streaming semantics, and error taxonomy. This is a customer-facing behavior change even where API surface remains the same. We need a coordinated communications plan that:
- reduces surprise
- avoids “Redwood is unstable” framing
- gives customers clear migration steps
- preempts support spikes during rollout

This ticket covers: release notes requirements, migration guide requirements, deprecation messaging, and announcement strategy.

## What is changing (customer-facing summary)
1) **Auth resolution order** is aligned across SDKs (explicit param/client option > env vars). Old env var names may be deprecated with warnings.
2) **Retry policy defaults** align: retries for 429, select 5xx, and network/transient errors; respect `Retry-After`; exponential backoff with jitter; consistent max attempts.
3) **Timeout model** aligns: consistent overall timeout and/or connect/read semantics per SDK; defaults may change.
4) **Streaming semantics** align: standardized disconnect errors, partial output handling, and cancellation behavior; streaming retries remain conservative (guidance + idempotency).
5) **Error taxonomy** aligns: typed errors include `request_id`, `status_code`, `retryable` flag, and error `code` where available.
6) **Observability/logging fields** become consistent (or are supported via hooks) to improve debug: `request_id`, `retry_count`, `timeout_ms`, `streaming_disconnect_reason`.

## Goals
- Ensure all SDK releases ship with consistent messaging and point to one canonical migration guide.
- Ensure release notes are explicit about behavior changes (timeouts/retries), with safe language and configuration guidance.
- Ensure deprecations are clearly called out with timelines (where applicable) and avoid hard breaks unless unavoidable.
- Provide support + CS with talk tracks and a short “How to troubleshoot” snippet (request_id, SDK version, retry/timeout config).

## Non-goals
- No new pricing/billing policy messaging here (unless required to clarify retry + idempotency concerns).
- No deep technical justification in announcement copy (link out to docs for details).

## Target audiences + channels
### A) Self-serve devs (PLG)
- Channels: docs site, SDK READMEs, GitHub release notes, in-console changelog (if available), #announcements post.
- Messaging: “More predictable defaults + better reliability tooling.” Emphasize consistency across languages.

### B) Enterprise/platform teams
- Channels: CS email template + CSM outreach, optional “heads-up” email for top accounts with heavy streaming usage.
- Messaging: “Safer retry behavior + request_id surfaced + better control knobs.” Include explicit note about conservative streaming retry.

### C) Support/on-call enablement
- Channels: Support playbook update + internal macro.
- Messaging: what to ask for (request_id, SDK version, endpoint path), which knobs to tune (timeouts, max attempts), when to disable retries.

## Deliverables
1) **Canonical migration guide** (docs)
- Must include:
  - What changed (bullet list + table if possible)
  - Deprecated options / env vars and replacements
  - Default values (old vs new) for retries/timeouts
  - “If you only do one thing” snippet: set explicit timeout + max attempts
  - Streaming-specific section: disconnects, partial output, cancellation, retry guidance + idempotency keys
  - Troubleshooting: request_id, retry_count logging, common 429/timeouts
- Location: Confluence + docs site (published). Draft currently tracked in: `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json`

2) **SDK release notes requirements (per repo)**
- Each SDK release notes must include:
  - Headline: “Standardized retries/timeouts/auth behavior across SDKs”
  - Breaking/behavior change callouts (timeouts + retries)
  - Link to migration guide
  - “How to keep old behavior” (if flags exist) OR “How to override defaults” (timeout/retry config)
  - Explicit statement: “Streaming requests are not automatically retried by default to avoid duplicate side effects; see guidance.”

3) **Deprecation messaging plan**
- If env var names changed:
  - Deprecate old names with warnings for at least one minor release cycle (where possible)
  - Provide a clear timeline in release notes + migration guide
  - Do not log secret values; warnings must be redaction-safe

4) **Announcement plan (don’t alarm customers)**
- One public announcement per SDK release window, plus a consolidated cross-language announcement once all three are stable.
- Draft copy principles:
  - Lead with “predictable, consistent behavior” and “better control and observability”
  - Avoid “retry storms”, “incident”, “bug” language
  - Include clear CTA: “Upgrade + skim migration guide; set explicit timeouts if you have strict SLOs.”
- Channels:
  - Docs “What’s new” / changelog
  - GitHub Releases
  - #announcements (internal + external-facing comms artifact)
  - Optional: targeted email for top enterprise accounts (CS-driven)

5) **Customer comms templates**
- A) Short upgrade note (CS email): 150–250 words + link to migration guide + top 3 FAQs.
- B) Support macro: request_id + SDK version + retry/timeout config snippet.

## Proposed messaging (draft)
### One-liner
“We’ve standardized retries, timeouts, streaming behavior, and error fields across our Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs for more predictable production behavior.”

### Key bullets
- Consistent retry + timeout defaults across SDKs
- Respects `Retry-After` on 429s
- Errors always surface `request_id` for faster support
- Streaming disconnect handling is clearer; retries remain opt-in / guidance-based to avoid duplicates

### FAQ candidates
- “Will this increase my usage/cost?” → Explain retry limits, respect Retry-After, and how to cap max attempts; advise idempotency patterns.
- “Why aren’t streaming requests automatically retried?” → Duplicate side effects/partial output; provide best practice guidance.
- “What do I need to change?” → Most users: nothing; production users: set explicit timeouts + max attempts.

## Rollout sequencing (comms)
- T-1 week (internal): share final copy in #docs + #support; support playbook updated.
- T-0 (beta): mention in beta release notes; ask 3–5 design partners to upgrade; capture feedback.
- Stable releases (per SDK): ship release notes + link migration guide.
- Consolidated announcement: once Python/TS/Go stable are out within ~1–2 weeks, publish “SDK parity v1” announcement.

## Success metrics
- Support tickets tagged “SDK timeouts/retries/streaming” down 20–30% within 4–6 weeks post-stable.
- Increased share of requests with request_id surfaced in customer logs (qualitative via support sampling).
- No significant increase in platform retry amplification (monitor via SRE dashboards).

## Open questions
1) Do we need explicit “potentially breaking” label for timeout default changes (per language)?
2) Do we have any customers relying on the old env var names heavily? (CS to confirm top accounts.)
3) Can we add a minimal in-console changelog entry for hosted API users upgrading SDKs? (Nice-to-have.)

- Retry/timeout standard: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json`
- Auth guidance: `sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sdk-auth-resolution-and-secret-handling.json`
- Migration guide draft: `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json`
- Streaming quickstart: `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/streaming-quickstart-consistent-behavior.json`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Migration guide published and linked from all three SDK release notes
- [ ] Release notes include explicit timeout + retry behavior change section
- [ ] Deprecation warnings (if any) have a documented timeline + replacement
- [ ] Support macro + playbook updated and reviewed by Support partner (Dev Patel)
- [ ] Final announcement copy approved by DevEx (Monica Patel) and Docs lead (Elliot Price)
comments: 2026-01-22 (Henry Cho): Drafted comms skeleton. Need confirmation from SDK owners on which changes are default vs behind flags for first stable release.
2026-01-24 (Elliot Price): Docs can support one canonical migration guide + per-language snippets. Please keep release notes concise and link out. Wei can help with final copy edits.
2026-02-03 (Dev Patel): Strong ask from Support: please add a short troubleshooting block (request_id + SDK version + how to disable retries). This will reduce back-and-forth.
2026-02-08 (Monica Patel): +1 to emphasizing consistency and “predictable defaults.” Avoid any phrasing that suggests prior SDKs were unsafe; frame as “standardization” and “more control knobs.”
2026-02-12 (Marcus Lin): Reminder: deprecation warnings must not print secret values or full env var contents. If referencing env vars, only name keys, never values.

2026-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE side, please explicitly mention that SDK respects Retry-After and uses jittered backoff; this is a reliability improvement, not just behavior churn. Also call out max attempts defaults in release notes to prevent misconfig.
2026-02-25 (Henry Cho): Marking In Review. Pending final confirmation of default timeout values per language + exact deprecation timeline for old env var names.
